Hello - sometimes in examples there is a -1 appearing after the y ~ f(.., "ar1")-1 like this. For example in slides 26-27 here: http://www.rni.helsinki.fi/~jmh/mrf08/R-INLA.pdf

Would someone be able to explain what this is for? Thanks!
Kathryn

On Thu, 2014-09-25 at 12:01 -0700, KTM wrote:

> Hello - sometimes in examples there is a -1 appearing after the y ~
> f(.., "ar1")-1 like this. For example in slides 26-27 here:
> http://www.rni.helsinki.fi/~jmh/mrf08/R-INLA.pdf
>
> Would someone be able to explain what this is for? Thanks!
> Kathryn

this is the same as for 'lm()' or 'glm()' and removes the intercept
which is default added.

so

y~x gives y = intercept + beta.x * x + `noise'

while

y~x-1 gives y = beta.x * x + `noise'

'-1' is the same as '0', so you can use either of the two.
